K1.text: Stateless HMAC cookie (8h TTL) with the staff row re-read each request: only deactivating the whole user invalidates sessions. There's no per-session row or watermark, and logout only deletes the client cookie, so a stolen cookie for an active user lasts until expiry. Manage tokens and API/MCP keys are stored hashed; sign-in is password via POST server action, no sign-in links. Checked by reading the session code. This is stricter than the 2026-11-10 ✔.
K1.gap_reason: Server-side revocation needs a session table or a per-user session watermark (e.g. sessionsValidAfter compared with a signed iat). That's a new session mechanism, which the brief says not to build. Needs an owner decision: build it or accept the risk in the decision log.
